chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is in his prayer and suspects that his garment has torn or that something has touched him; is it permissible for him to look at it or touch it? He said: 'If it is at the front of his garment or on its sides, there is no harm; but if it is at the back, he should not turn back, for it is not permissible.'
ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they suspect their garment is torn during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in prayer, ruling that minor defects at the front or sides do not break concentration (*khushu*) enough to require immediate checking, whereas a defect at the back necessitates maintaining the current posture to avoid invalidating the prayer through excessive movement. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual purity with the practical ease of the worshipper, ensuring that doubt does not unduly burden the validity of the act of worship.
